bullets.text: Built a C++17 order book and matching engine that replayed 50.9M real IEX DEEP+ messages with no resync, matching 99,122 of 99,123 fills exactly and 100% of top-of-book prices
Sustained 1.26M events/sec end-to-end, averaging 686.7 ns/event with the CPU fixed at its 1.40 GHz base clock; full matching takes 1.41× the time of a mirror-only book
Traced a 1.65× phantom regression to a CPU-governor artifact using perf counters and a null control book; core pinning and a fixed clock cut run-to-run variance from 6% to 0.06%
Benchmarked B+ tree vs LSM skip-list stores for the replay's event log on 2M-record workloads (B+ tree: 12.8× read throughput for 27% more disk); documented adaptive batch sizing as a negative result
Writing Java policies that tune upper/lower bounds on EC2 capacity reserved for Amazon Redshift operations like patching, balancing availability against cost; initial backtests complete
Precomputed a tree-style search index over popular workflows from a 270K+ row PostgreSQL table (Python/SQLAlchemy, Redis cache) to minimize DB queries under access limits
Cut LLM workflow generation time 65% to under 15s by decomposing a Claude skill into sub-skills backed by Python search/validation tools, guided by CloudWatch + OpenSearch latency logs
Reduced end-to-end latency 34% for a pipeline routing 6,000+ scraped research documents to inference by replacing S3 staging hops with Kinesis streams feeding Lambda
Built a Python pipeline for PhysTwin, a PhD-led digital twin targeting ICLR, running AnyGrasp on multi-camera images and rendering grasps as Open3D overlays for a VLM; tuned its detection prompts

Co-founded a 110+ member campus product studio that has shipped 5 live products, including Tortuga, a class scheduler with 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days; built Redis caching for its Prisma ORM queries
